--- title: "Model 1 — XGBoost" subtitle: "Gradient-boosted trees, the Kaggle workhorse" --- > **Where we are:** First of six model documents in the > [House Prices — Tidymodels Tour](../index.qmd). All six follow the *same* > structure — recipe → spec → workflow → tune → finalize → evaluate → save — so > once you've read this one, the others are quick to skim for the differences. > The features come from the [EDA](01-eda.qmd) and the shared `make_recipe()`. > Remember the project-wide convention: **we model `log(SalePrice)`**, because > Kaggle scores this competition as RMSE on the log scale (see the > [master document](../index.qmd)). ## Why XGBoost first? Gradient-boosted decision trees are the default first reach on tabular Kaggle problems. They handle mixed numeric/categorical features, capture interactions (quality × size, neighborhood × age) automatically, are robust to monotone transforms, and tune to strong accuracy with modest effort. We tune four of the most impactful knobs. ## Setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Project setup: tidyverse + tidymodels, seed = 42, paths, parallel backend. source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R")) # Shared feature engineering: defines make_recipe(data). source(here("R", "02_features.R")) library(tidyverse) library(tidymodels) library(here) library(vip) # variable importance plots library(xgboost) # the engine ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Model the LOG of SalePrice — this is the scale Kaggle scores on, so training # with RMSE here directly optimises the leaderboard metric. train <- readr::read_csv(here("data", "processed", "train.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(SalePrice = log(SalePrice)) ``` ::: ## The recipe The shared recipe encodes everything we justified in the [EDA](01-eda.qmd): impute `LotFrontage`, Yeo-Johnson the skewed areas, lump rare factor levels, dummy-encode, drop the `Id`, and append principal components. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xgb_recipe <- make_recipe(train) xgb_recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ── Recipe all_numeric_predictors() ``` ::: ::: ## The model specification We mark the four tuning parameters with `tune()`. tidymodels fills them in during the grid search. Note `set_mode("regression")`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xgb_spec <- boost_tree( trees = tune(), tree_depth = tune(), learn_rate = tune(), min_n = tune() ) |> set_engine("xgboost") |> set_mode("regression") xgb_spec ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Boosted Tree Model Specification (regression) Main Arguments: trees = tune() min_n = tune() tree_depth = tune() learn_rate = tune() Computational engine: xgboost ``` ::: ::: ## The workflow A `workflow` bundles the recipe and the model so resampling applies the *exact* same preprocessing to every fold — no leakage. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xgb_wf <- workflow() |> add_recipe(xgb_recipe) |> add_model(xgb_spec) ``` ::: ## Tuning with 10-fold cross-validation ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Stratify on the (log) outcome so each fold spans the full price range. set.seed(42) folds <- vfold_cv(train, v = 10, strata = SalePrice) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Predictors used to finalize data-dependent params (num_comp upper bound). preds <- prep(make_recipe(train, num_comp = 2)) |> bake(new_data = NULL) |> select(-SalePrice, -Id) xgb_params <- extract_parameter_set_dials(xgb_wf) |> finalize(preds) |> update(num_comp = num_comp(range = c(2L, 15L))) set.seed(42) xgb_grid <- grid_space_filling(xgb_params, size = 20) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Score every candidate on RMSE (the competition metric on the log scale) and # R-squared (interpretable goodness-of-fit). xgb_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, rsq) set.seed(42) xgb_tuned <- tune_grid( xgb_wf, resamples = folds, grid = xgb_grid, metrics = xgb_metrics, control = control_grid(save_pred = TRUE, save_workflow = TRUE) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} saveRDS(xgb_tuned, here("models", "xgboost_res.rds")) ``` ::: ### Tuning results ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} autoplot(xgb_tuned, metric = "rmse") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![RMSE across the tuning grid for each hyperparameter (autoplot).](02-xgboost_files/figure-html/tune-plot-1.png){width=864} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # The top candidates by RMSE (lower is better). show_best(xgb_tuned, metric = "rmse", n = 5) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ## Finalize and fit on the full training set ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} best_xgb <- select_best(xgb_tuned, metric = "rmse") best_xgb ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} final_xgb_wf <- finalize_workflow(xgb_wf, best_xgb) # Fit the finalized workflow on ALL the training data — the model we ship. set.seed(42) xgb_fit <- fit(final_xgb_wf, data = train) ``` ::: ## Cross-validated performance The fairest estimate of out-of-sample skill is the CV score of the chosen configuration — not the fit on the full training data (which overfits by construction). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} collect_metrics(xgb_tuned) |> semi_join(best_xgb, by = names(best_xgb)) |> select(.metric, mean, std_err, n) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip} The `rmse` here is on the **log(SalePrice)** scale — the same units Kaggle reports on the leaderboard. These CV metrics feed the results table on the [master document](../index.qmd) automatically. ::: ### Observed vs predicted (out-of-fold) Built from the held-out CV predictions for the best configuration — so it reflects generalization, not memorization. Points on the diagonal are perfect. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} collect_predictions(xgb_tuned) |> filter(.config == best_xgb$.config) |> ggplot(aes(x = SalePrice, y = .pred)) + geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linetype = 2) + geom_point(alpha = 0.35, colour = house_pal[1]) + labs(title = "XGBoost — CV predicted vs observed", x = "Observed log(SalePrice)", y = "Predicted log(SalePrice)") + coord_equal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Out-of-fold predicted vs observed log(SalePrice).](02-xgboost_files/figure-html/obs-pred-1.png){width=528} ::: ::: ### Variable importance ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} xgb_fit |> extract_fit_parsnip() |> vip(num_features = 15, geom = "col", aesthetics = list(fill = house_pal[1])) + labs(title = "XGBoost variable importance") + theme_minimal() ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Top features by XGBoost gain. Quality and size dominate.](02-xgboost_files/figure-html/vip-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: `OverallQual`, `GrLivArea`, the engineered `TotalSF`, and neighborhood/age features sit at the top — exactly the signal the [EDA](01-eda.qmd) surfaced. ## Save the fitted workflow ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} saveRDS(xgb_fit, file = here("models", "xgboost_fit.rds")) ``` ::: ## Submission Generate this model's leaderboard CSV with the **parameterized** [submission document](submission.qmd): ```bash quarto render docs/submission.qmd -P model:xgboost ``` That loads `models/xgboost_fit.rds`, predicts on the test set, **exponentiates** back to dollars, and writes `models/submission_xgboost.csv` (columns `Id`, `SalePrice`). See the [Kaggle setup guide](setup-kaggle.md) for authentication. ## Next steps - Compare against the **[Random Forest](03-random-forest.qmd)** — a robust, almost-no-tuning baseline. - Then the **[Neural Net](04-neural-net.qmd)**, **[Elastic Net](06-elasticnet.qmd)**, **[SVM](07-svm.qmd)** and **[MARS](08-mars.qmd)**. - Record this model's CV scores in the **[master results table](../index.qmd)**.
